stimuli.title: Seven employees hold seven distinct ranks (rank 1 is junior-most and rank 7 is senior-most).
stimuli.body:
Clues:

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain S ≥ Q < T = U ≤ P, decide which conclusions follow. I: Q < T. II: U = P.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is always true and II is not necessarily true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain Z > U > T = X < P, decide which conclusions follow. I: U ≥ X. II: T < P.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is always true and II is always true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain S ≤ V > T ≥ X < R, decide which conclusions follow. I: S ≥ R. II: X ≤ R.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain W > R = X > Q > Z, decide which conclusions follow. I: W ≥ R. II: R ≥ Q.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain S > T ≤ X ≤ V > R, decide which conclusions follow. I: X ≤ V. II: V ≥ R.

questions.stem: Statements: All painters are teachers. Some runners are painters. Conclusions: I. Some runners are teachers. II. Some teachers are runners. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The existing C∩A members must lie in B, proving both conclusions.

questions.stem: Statements: No pilots are sailors. All artists are sailors. Some artists are sailors. Conclusions: I. No pilots are artists. II. Some artists are not pilots. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: All C members belong to B, disjoint from A; some C are explicitly given.

questions.stem: Statements: Some drivers are teachers. Some teachers are runners. Conclusions: I. Some drivers are runners. II. All runners are drivers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.explanation: The specified intersections do not force A and C to overlap or include one another.

questions.stem: Statements: Some pilots are poets. All poets are bakers. Conclusions: I. Some pilots are bakers. II. All pilots are bakers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Some A–B members must be C; not all A need be C.

questions.stem: Statements: No coders are painters. Some painters are poets. Conclusions: I. Some poets are not coders. II. No poets are coders. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The B∩C members are outside A; other C members remain unrestricted.

questions.stem: Ritu walks 10 km north, then 8 km east, then 2 km south and finally 2 km west. What is her shortest distance from the starting point?

questions.stem: A cyclist travels 18 km north, 8 km east, 10 km south and 2 km west. What total distance did the cyclist travel?
